'''Armed conflicts and attacks'''
*[[Gaza war]]
**[[Israeli invasion of the Gaza Strip]], [[2025 Gaza City offensive]]
***At least 53 [[Palestinians]] are killed by [[Israel]]i attacks, including 35 in [[Gaza City]] where the [[IDF|Israeli army]] has been concentrating its assault. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/liveblog/2025/9/14/live-qatar-hosts-muslim-leaders-summit-israel-continues-gaza-city-attacks (Al Jazeera)]
*[[Colombian conflict]]
**A [[National Police of Colombia|police]] officer is killed and four others are injured in an attack on a police station in [[Cauca Department|Cauca]], [[Colombia]], by [[FARC dissidents]], prompting [[Military Forces of Colombia|military]] deployment to restore order. [https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/world/rest-of-world/colombia-cop-killed-4-four-injured-in-attack-on-carmelo-station-led-by-defunct-group-farc/articleshow/123887775.cms (''The Times of India'')]
*[[Islamist insurgency in Niger]]
**The [[Niger]]ien [[Government of Niger|government]] reports that at least fourteen [[Niger Armed Forces|soldiers]] were killed in ambushes by unknown militants in the [[Tillabéri Region]] last week. [https://apnews.com/article/niger-attack-islamic-state-066e2cee314cec0b09562f547fb3b08a (AP)]

'''Arts and culture'''
*[[77th Primetime Emmy Awards]]
**At the 2025 [[Primetime Emmy Awards]] in the [[United States]], ''[[The Studio (TV series)|The Studio]]'' becomes the most-nominated first-year comedy series in the awards' history at 23 nominations, tying ''[[The Bear (TV series)|The Bear's]]'' nominations from [[76th Primetime Emmy Awards|last year]]. [https://variety.com/2025/tv/news/the-studio-emmys-record-most-nominations-season-1-1236448864/ (''Variety'')]
**For the first time in the awards' history, every nominee for [[Primetime Emmy Award for Outstanding Writing for a Comedy Series|Outstanding Writing for a Comedy Series]] has at least one woman on the writing team. [https://variety.com/2025/tv/awards/emmys-2025-diversity-worst-showing-actors-color-1236448971/ (''Variety'')]
**''The Studio'' wins [[Primetime Emmy Award for Outstanding Comedy Series|Outstanding Comedy Series]] and ''[[The Pitt]]'' wins [[Primetime Emmy Award for Outstanding Drama Series|Outstanding Drama Series]], while ''[[Adolescence (TV series)|Adolescence]]'' wins [[Primetime Emmy Award for Outstanding Limited or Anthology Series|Outstanding Limited or Anthology Series]]. [https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/lists/emmy-winners-2025-list/ (''The Hollywood Reporter'')]
**[[English people|English]] actor [[Owen Cooper (actor)|Owen Cooper]] wins the [[Primetime Emmy Award for Outstanding Supporting Actor in a Limited or Anthology Series or Movie]] for his role in ''Adolescence'', becoming the youngest male recipient of an [[Emmy Awards|Emmy Award]]. [https://tribune.net.ph/2025/09/15/owen-cooper-makes-history-as-youngest-ever-male-emmy-winner (''Daily Tribune'')]
**[[Tramell Tillman]] becomes the first [[Black people|Black man]] to win the award for [[Primetime Emmy Award for Outstanding Supporting Actor in a Drama Series|Outstanding Supporting Actor in a Drama Series]] for his work in ''[[Severance (TV series)|Severance]]''. [https://variety.com/2025/tv/awards/tramell-tillman-first-black-supporting-winner-history-1236509585/ (''Variety'')]
**The [[Bob Hope Humanitarian Award]] is awarded to married actors [[Ted Danson]] and [[Mary Steenburgen]] in recognition of "a lifetime of philanthropy", marking the first time the award is presented to a couple. [https://www.televisionacademy.com/features/news/awards-news/bob-hope-humanitarian-250730 (Television Academy)]

'''Health and environment'''
*[[2025 Kasaï Province Ebola outbreak]]
**The [[World Health Organization]] begins [[Ebola]] [[Ebola vaccine|vaccinations]] for exposed individuals and health workers in [[Kasaï Province]], [[Democratic Republic of the Congo]]. [https://apnews.com/article/congo-ebola-vaccine-who-06f642e38778fbe4f095490bb102a621 (AP)]

'''Politics and elections'''
*[[2025 Turkish protests]]
**Over 50,000 people march in [[Ankara]], [[Turkey]], to protest against and call for [[President of Turkey|President]] [[Recep Tayyip Erdoğan]] to resign following the [[Government of Turkey|government's]] judicial [[coup]] against the country's opposition party, [[Republican People's Party]], and its leader [[Özgür Özel]]. [https://www.dw.com/en/turkey-thousands-protest-against-crackdown-on-opposition/a-73992893 (DW)]
*[[Algeria]]n [[President of Algeria|president]] [[Abdelmadjid Tebboune]] appoints [[Sifi Ghrieb]] as [[Prime Minister of Algeria|prime minister]] following [[Nadir Larbaoui]]'s dismissal in August. [https://www.reuters.com/world/africa/algerian-president-appoints-new-prime-minister-energy-minister-2025-09-14/ (Reuters)]

'''Sports'''
*[[2025 Vuelta a España]]
**[[Sport in Denmark|Danish]] rider [[Jonas Vingegaard]] wins the annual [[Vuelta a España]] [[road cycling]] race in [[Spain]]. [https://www.lemonde.fr/en/sports/article/2025/09/14/vuelta-vingegaard-crowned-champion-as-final-stage-is-cancelled-because-of-pro-palestine-protests-in-madrid_6745397_9.html (''Le Monde'')]
**The final stage of the race is suspended following [[Gaza war protests#Spain|pro-Palestinian protests]] against the [[Israel–Premier Tech]] team on [[Paseo del Prado]] in [[Madrid]]. [https://edition.cnn.com/2025/09/14/europe/spain-cycling-protest-vuelta-gaza-israel-latam-intl (CNN)]
*[[EuroBasket 2025]]
**In [[basketball]], [[Germany men's national basketball team|Germany]] defeats [[Turkey men's national basketball team|Turkey]] 88–83 in the [[EuroBasket 2025 final]], with [[Dennis Schröder]] selected as the [[FIBA EuroBasket MVP|MVP]]. In the third-place match, [[Greece men's national basketball team|Greece]] beats [[Finland men's national basketball team|Finland]]. [https://www.fiba.basketball/en/events/fiba-eurobasket-2025/games/123033-TUR-GER (FIBA)]
